Well yer. Of course they did, and they will continue to do so for a period. That's literally what happens in a bubble. Stocks keep going up and up at a rapid rate because more and more people get caught up in the overhype and invest more and more. (I.e. the bubble expands). 

Until the day comes when the stocks are way too high-priced and overvalued. The companies don't make the huge, overhyped profits investors expected, so stocks don't deliver. The overhype is exposed, reality suddenly kicks in. People realise the stocks high value is overinflated fake hype,

People begin to become aware that they invested far too much of their money in the overhyped, fake-inflated-value stocks that will not deliver anything like the returns they thought they were going to get. They panic sell the stocks, which cause them to dip, new buyers see this dip and become to afaid to invest which cause the stocks to dip even more. 

This causes the panic to spread. More and more people see the stock prices going down alongside realising the exposure of the overhype fake and so more and more people panic sell and more and more people refuse to buy. Such that the stock value and prices keeps falling and falling at a rapid rate. 

The panic ultimately rapidly spreads so much and so quickly that the point is reached where demand for the stocks hits zero, and the price of the stocks plunges vertically in a matter hours and/or even in a matter of minutes, resulting in a complete crash of the stocks. (I.e. the bubble bursts). 

All those still unfortunate enough to be invested (which is mostly ordinary people who have little to no clue about investing, but simply invested far too much of their money because they followed the crowd and fell for the overhype that they would make big returns and couldn't lose). Lose everything. 

This is exactly what caused the stock market bubble crash of 1929, the dot-com (internet) bubble crash of 2000 and the housing/subprime mortgage bubble crash of 2008.

The same thing is now underway with AI. AI and associated peripheral tech are overhyped and overvalued too F-bomb, but most people haven't realised yet and are still falling for the hype and investing their money (expanding the bubble).

Your logic here is completely flawed mate. You can’t acknowledge a K-shaped economy in one sentence, and then say the best move is to blindly buy a broad market index. A K-shaped environment means the lower half of the economy is deteriorating meaning a generic stock basket forces you to hold the dying bottom half of that 'K' curve. Also, saying the market is a guaranteed inflation hedge completely ignores valuation compression. When inflation is rampant, central banks hike interest rates, which directly drives up corporate borrowing costs and compresses price-to-earnings (P/E) multiples. If you want an example, severe inflationary cycles (like the 1970s) produced a 'lost decade' where the broad stock market dramatically underperformed in real terms. The real protection against rampant inflation requires targeting specific hard assets (gold/silver/productive farmland), commodities, or elite companies with genuine pricing power not just crossing your fingers and hoping a broad index bails you out mate.

Automation, AI, and the Transition to a Post-Labor Society
Nearly 70% of GDP in modern economies is driven by consumer spending. This creates a fundamental question for the future:
What happens if automation and AI eliminate large numbers of jobs, and consumers no longer have the income needed to participate in the economy?
If consumers lose purchasing power, businesses lose customers. If businesses lose customers, companies fail. Eventually, even the wealthy are affected because the entire economic system begins to contract.
One possible solution is not to resist automation, but to adapt civilization to it intelligently.
Tax the Robots: A Transitional Economic Model
Employees are expensive. From a business pective, robots and AI systems make economic sense because they can dramatically reduce costs while increasing efficiency and productivity.
However, there is a systemic contradiction: The same automation that increases corporate profits may simultaneously reduce the purchasing power of consumers.
A modern economy cannot function if productivity rises while consumer income collapses.
One possible solution is a robotic taxation system designed not to punish innovation, but to stabilize society during the transition toward a post-labor economy.
If a portion of the enormous productivity gains from automation were redistributed back into society, several things could happen simultaneously:
Companies would still benefit from massive efficiency gains.
Citizens could maintain purchasing power.
The cost of living could be reduced.
Consumer demand would remain stable.
Economies could avoid large-scale instability caused by technological unemployment.
In the long term, both companies and workers benefit.
This is not anti-technology. It is pro-stability, pro-human, and ultimately pro-civilization.
Humans Did Not Evolve for Industrial Labor Systems
Another issue rarely discussed is whether modern labor systems are psychologically compatible with human beings.
Humans did not evolve for endless industrial schedules, long commutes, or extreme work cultures such as the Chinese “996” system: 9 AM to 9 PM, 6 days a week.
Such systems create chronic stress, anxiety, burnout, and long-term damage to mental and physical health.
Anthropological studies of hunter-gatherer societies — social groups much closer to the conditions under which humans evolved — suggest a very different pattern of life.
Within communities roughly aligned with the Dunbar number of approximately 150 individuals, hunter-gatherers often spent the equivalent of about 40 hours weekly securing food and necessities. However, this was spread over seven days, averaging closer to 5.7 hours per day.
More importantly, these activities were frequently social, cooperative, and meaningful. Hunting, fishing, gathering, storytelling, and tool-making were integrated into daily life rather than separated into something psychologically experienced as “work.”
The modern division between “living” and “working” may itself be historically unnatural.
Automation Could Improve Human Life
Automation and AI also have the potential to dramatically improve quality of life beyond economics alone.
For example, autonomous vehicles could:
reduce traffic deaths,
lower insurance and healthcare costs,
reduce commuting stress,
save enormous amounts of time,
and improve overall public safety.
Combined with robotics and AI-assisted productivity, humanity may eventually move toward a civilization where survival no longer depends upon exhausting labor simply to meet basic needs.
The real challenge is not whether this transformation is coming.
The real challenge is whether humanity managems the transition wisely — or attempts to force industrial-age economic systems to operate in a world where intelligent machines can increasingly replace human labor.
There are many additional implications and considerations, but it is important to address one issue at a time to avoid losing sight of the central problem.

Well yer. Of course they did, and they will continue to do so for a period. That's literally what happens in a bubble. Stocks keep going up and up at a rapid rate because more and more people get caught up in the overhype and invest more and more. (I.e. the bubble expands). 

Until the day comes when the stocks are way too high-priced and overvalued. The companies don't make the huge, overhyped profits investors expected, so stocks don't deliver. The overhype is exposed, reality suddenly kicks in. People realise the stocks high value is overinflated fake hype,

People begin to become aware that they invested far too much of their money in the overhyped, fake-inflated-value stocks that will not deliver anything like the returns they thought they were going to get. They panic sell the stocks, which cause them to dip, new buyers see this dip and become to afaid to invest which cause the stocks to dip even more. 

This causes the panic to spread. More and more people see the stock prices going down alongside realising the exposure of the overhype fake and so more and more people panic sell and more and more people refuse to buy. Such that the stock value and prices keeps falling and falling at a rapid rate. 

The panic ultimately rapidly spreads so much and so quickly that the point is reached where demand for the stocks hits zero, and the price of the stocks plunges vertically in a matter hours and/or even in a matter of minutes, resulting in a complete crash of the stocks. (I.e. the bubble bursts). 

All those still unfortunate enough to be invested (which is mostly ordinary people who have little to no clue about investing, but simply invested far too much of their money because they followed the crowd and fell for the overhype that they would make big returns and couldn't lose). Lose everything. 

This is exactly what caused the stock market bubble crash of 1929, the dot-com (internet) bubble crash of 2000 and the housing/subprime mortgage bubble crash of 2008.

Your logic here is completely flawed mate. You can’t acknowledge a K-shaped economy in one sentence, and then say the best move is to blindly buy a broad market index. A K-shaped environment means the lower half of the economy is deteriorating meaning a generic stock basket forces you to hold the dying bottom half of that 'K' curve. Also, saying the market is a guaranteed inflation hedge completely ignores valuation compression. When inflation is rampant, central banks hike interest rates, which directly drives up corporate borrowing costs and compresses price-to-earnings (P/E) multiples. If you want an example, severe inflationary cycles (like the 1970s) produced a 'lost decade' where the broad stock market dramatically underperformed in real terms. The real protection against rampant inflation requires targeting specific hard assets (gold/silver/productive farmland), commodities, or elite companies with genuine pricing power not just crossing your fingers and hoping a broad index bails you out mate.
